Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}(x{e}^{2x}){|}_{0}^{1/2}-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(x{e}^{2x}){|}_{0}^{1/2}-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}{|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2(1/2)}-0\cdot {e}^{2\cdot 0}]-\frac{1}{4}[{e}^{2(1/2)}-{e}^{2\cdot 0}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{e}{2}-0]-\frac{1}{4}[e-1] \\  & =\frac{e}{4}-\frac{e-1}{4} \\  & =\frac{e-e+1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
